design:
Tier 1: UI over routes that exist, plus one field. No migration, no Hub-restart hazard.

Decisions (operator, 2026-11-06): opened from the conversation's menu and from the Traces view narrowed to one conversation; long idle gaps folded; a carried-over conversation shows its own turns and links to the one it continued; mocked before building.

From the mock (author, 2026-11-06, against three recorded conversations of 17-24 turns):
- Gaps over 20 minutes fold. 10 minutes produced 16 breaks in a two-day conversation, and the axis labels piled up.
- An unfolded turn's spans are drawn on the turn's own scale, in a tinted track with a line saying so. On the conversation's axis they were 1-pixel slivers.
- Axis labels that would overlap are dropped from the drawing and kept in hover text.
- 'from you' marks the turns the operator started. Runs record only operator or autonomous, so the others carry no label rather than an internal word.

Data: the list route with conversation_id already returns each run's row (start, end, cost, model, status) and /totals the statistics; a turn range is a since/until pair on both. The run's initiator (aw.run.initiator on the root span) is not in the list's row yet. Spans come from /traces/by-run/{run_id} when a turn is unfolded.

CURRENT   conversation -> 'Trace of the latest run' -> one run
PROPOSED  conversation -> 'Trace of this conversation' -> turns on one axis, gaps folded -> unfold a turn -> its spans on its own scale -> span detail

checked: hub/hub/api/v1/traces.py:41-70 selects runs by conversation_id for both the list and /totals routes, and both take since/until.
hub/ui/src/components/traces/ holds the traces view, one run's waterfall (bars relative to the one trace) and the drawer.

Operator's Hub, mode=ro, 2026-11-06: 1,711 runs in 1,193 conversations; the largest has 24 runs over about 18 hours; spans per trace average 5.5, maximum 511; aw.run.initiator is 'operator' (424) or 'autonomous' (1,224).
The mock (hub/ui/mock, #conversation-trace) draws three recorded conversations (24, 17 and 21 turns; the first carried over from the third) with the components the build wires.
limits: The mock reads recorded fixtures, not the routes; paging past 200 runs and request counts are not exercised by it.
No requirement is demonstrated yet: the acceptance drive is proposed coverage, to be written and recorded failing before the build.

tasks.title: Conversation trace totals show tool errors (F1147, FR-6)

open_questions.question: Where is it opened from? Answered (operator, 2026-11-06): the conversation's menu, and the Traces view narrowed to one conversation.
Idle gaps? Answered (operator, 2026-11-06): folded into marked breaks, no to-scale switch.
A carried-over conversation? Answered (operator, 2026-11-06): only its own turns, with a link to the earlier conversation's trace.

Mock first? Answered (operator, 2026-11-06): yes; mocked the same day in hub/ui/mock (#conversation-trace). Its choices — the 20-minute fold, spans drawn on their turn's own scale, the 24h/6h/1h start choices — are the author's and stand until the operator changes them on review.

problem: A run is a trace today: each turn of a conversation is its own trace, opened one at a time from a per-turn link, the task story, the ledger or the Traces view (hub/ui/src/components/traces/TraceDrawer.tsx, opened from ten screens). The Traces view can filter to one conversation (hub/hub/api/v1/traces.py:59, conversation_id) and total it (/traces/totals), but it lists the runs as separate rows; nothing draws them together. So the questions a conversation raises — where its time went across turns, which turn got expensive, what the agent was doing between two answers — mean opening runs one by one and comparing them by hand. On the operator's Hub (read-only, 2026-11-06) conversations run up to 24 runs over about 18 hours, and a two-day conversation has turns spread across mornings and evenings; a single run's trace holds up to 511 spans.

requirements.statement: A conversation with at least one run offers 'Trace of this conversation' in its menu, and the Traces view narrowed to one conversation offers to open that conversation as one trace; both open the same view of that conversation.

The view shows every run of the conversation as a numbered turn, in the order the runs started, each placed on one time axis shared by all turns, with its start time, its cost when priced, 'from you' when the operator started it, and its duration; a turn still running is drawn open and grows.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-06: a conversation that spans a night drawn to scale is slivers; folding keeps every turn readable.
requirements.statement: A stretch longer than 20 minutes in which no turn of the conversation was running is drawn as a break of fixed width, marked across every row and labelled in the axis with its length; turns and shorter gaps are drawn to scale; axis labels that would overlap are left out of the drawing and kept in the hover text of their tick or break.

requirements.rationale: On the conversation's axis a ten-minute turn of a day-long conversation is a sliver, and its spans would be invisible (seen in the mock, 2026-11-06).
requirements.statement: A turn unfolds to show its spans as the single-run trace shows them (nested, named, coloured by kind), drawn across that turn's own duration rather than the conversation's axis, with a line saying so; selecting a turn or a span shows its detail below the timeline.

The operator narrows the view to a range of turns (from one turn to another) and to turns that started within the last 24 hours, 6 hours or hour, or at any time; the timeline, its breaks and the totals are redrawn over the turns that remain, a narrowed view offers to show every turn again, and a narrowing that leaves no turn says so.

Above the timeline the view totals the turns shown: how many of the conversation's turns, the time they were running and the time from the first one's start to the last one's end, their cost with the count of unpriced turns left out, their errors as failed turns and tool errors, and their model calls, tool calls and time waiting on the operator.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-06: each conversation's trace keeps a clear boundary; a chain of carry-overs would otherwise grow without limit.
requirements.statement: The trace of a conversation carried over from an earlier one shows only its own turns, names the conversation it continued, and opens that conversation's trace from there.

requirements.rationale: A conversation of 24 turns can hold over 10,000 spans; the turn rows answer most questions without them.
requirements.statement: Opening the view reads the conversation's turn rows and totals without reading every turn's spans; a turn's spans are read when it is first unfolded, and a turn whose trace was cleared or never recorded unfolds to a line saying it has no trace.

in_scope: Opening one trace of a whole conversation from the conversation's menu, and from the Traces view narrowed to one conversation
Every turn of the conversation on one timeline, long idle gaps folded into marked breaks
Unfolding a turn to see its spans, and any row's detail
Narrowing to a range of turns or a start time, with the drawing and totals following
Naming the conversation a carried-over one continued, and opening its trace
non_goals: Several agents or conversations on one timeline (slice 'woven-traces')
Including the turns of the conversation a carried-over one continued in its own trace (operator, 2026-11-06)
A switch to draw the idle gaps to scale (operator, 2026-11-06: folded)
Changing what the Hub records as spans
Trace retention, export, download and clearing
Runs of other conversations the agent delegated to or was handed by

summary: From a conversation, the operator opens one trace covering its turns on one timeline, narrows it to a range of turns or a start time, and unfolds a turn to see its spans, instead of opening one run's trace at a time. Long idle gaps are folded into marked breaks. Slice 2 of 'Checkpoints and traces you can find and use'; builds on the traces view (slice 1, built). Mocked 2026-11-06 against three recorded conversations.
